options.name: Progression Balancing
options.doc:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.
options.doc_html:

options.name: Accessibility
options.doc:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.
options.doc_html:

options.name: Include Shortcuts
options.doc:
Add the shortcut crystals as locations.

Buying a shortcut crystal checks a location instead of unlocking the
shortcut; Progressive Shortcut items unlock them instead.
options.doc_fr:
Ajoutez les cristaux de raccourci comme emplacements.

Acheter un cristal raccourci vérifie un emplacement au lieu de déverrouiller le raccourci; les éléments raccourcis progressifs les déverrouillent à la place.

options.name: Include Level Clears
options.doc:
Add a location for clearing each of levels 1-10.

A level counts as cleared when you take its exit portal, whether you
killed the Guardian or opened the portal with keys.
options.doc_fr:
Ajouter un emplacement pour nettoyer chacun des niveaux 1 à 10.

Un niveau compte comme dégagé lorsque vous prenez son portail de sortie, que vous ayez tué le Gardien ou ouvert le portail avec des clés.

options.name: Shop Upgrade Tiers
options.doc:
How many upgrades each of the three hub shops sells.

The Blacksmith, Apothecary and Monk each sell this many tiers, so this is
also three locations and three progression items per tier. Vanilla-style
play is 15; the default of 20 spreads the same power over more checks.

options.name: Shop Price Per Tier
options.doc:
Coins a hub shop's price climbs per tier already bought.

The Nth purchase from a shop costs N times this. Vanilla is 25, so the
first upgrade is 25 coins and the tenth is 250.
options.doc_fr:
Pièces de monnaie d'une boutique de hub grimpe par niveau déjà acheté.

L'achat Nth d'un magasin coûte N fois. Vanilla a 25 ans, donc la première mise à niveau est 25 pièces et la dixième est 250.

options.name: Shop Price Cliff
options.doc:
Extra coins-per-tier added every 10 tiers bought.

Vanilla raises the per-tier rate by 25 for every 10 upgrades you already
own, which is the sudden price wall in the back half of a shop. It could
only fire once at vanilla's 15-tier cap; with Archipelago's deeper shops
it fires two or three times, so the default here is 0 -- a purely linear
curve. Set it to 25 for the vanilla wall, or higher to make depth hurt
more.

options.name: Level Locks
options.doc:
Require an item before the hero may descend into each level.

On (the default), levels 2-11 are locked and Progressive Level Access
items open them in order. Taking the exit portal of a level whose
successor is still locked still counts that level as cleared, but drops
you back into the village with your hero, coins and unlocks intact --
the descent simply stops there until Archipelago says otherwise.

Off, every level is open from the start and only the shop-upgrade curve
gates how deep the logic expects you to get.

options.name: Shrine Checks Per Level
options.doc:
How many shrines on each level are Archipelago locations.

Shrines spawn at random through a level and always do exactly what they
always did; the first this many you activate on a level also check a
location. After that the level is out of Archipelago slots and its shrines
are back to being ordinary shrines.

0 turns the feature off entirely.

options.name: Trap Fill Percentage
options.doc:
Percentage of the leftover filler slots that become traps instead.

Only the slots no progression or skill item wanted are affected, so this
never displaces anything that matters. At 0 there are no traps at all.

options.name: Death Link
options.doc: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.
options.doc_html: When you die, everyone who enabled death link dies. Of course, the reverse is true too.
options.doc_fr: Quand vous mourez, tous ceux qui ont permis la mort meurent. Bien sûr, l'inverse est vrai aussi.
options.doc_html_fr: Quand vous mourez, tous ceux qui ont permis la mort meurent. Bien sûr, l'inverse est vrai aussi.

options.name: Death Amnesty Multiplier
options.doc:
Send only one DeathLink out of every this many deaths.

Vertical Drop Heroes is a roguelite and a hero dies every few minutes, so
an unfiltered DeathLink is a firehose pointed at the rest of the
multiworld. At 5, four deaths are yours alone and the fifth is everyone's.

0 and 1 both mean every death is sent. Deaths that an incoming DeathLink
caused never count toward this -- only deaths you earned yourself.

Has no effect unless death_link is on, and it filters only what you SEND:
every DeathLink other worlds send still kills your hero.

options.name: Death Amnesty Buffer
options.doc:
Send nothing at all for this many deaths, once per multiworld.

Grace while you are learning the game: the first this many deaths are
swallowed outright, and only afterwards does the multiplier start counting.
The count is per seed and slot and survives quitting the game, so it is a
one-off allowance for the whole multiworld, not a fresh one per session.
